item.research_question: Can high entropy oxide materials be designed to be water-resistant and exhibit excellent catalytic performance?
item.processing_route: Mechanochemical method using ball milling, followed by calcination at 550 °C for 2 h
item.test_conditions: C3H6 oxidation reaction in dry and humid conditions (4.2 vol% H2O)
key_findings: High entropy oxide materials exhibit better water resistance and catalytic performance compared to single metal oxides
The (Ni0.2Mg0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2Co0.2)Cr2O4 material shows excellent water resistance (>100 h) in C3H6 oxidation
The material has a lower T90 (265 °C) compared to single metal oxides (318-350 °C) in dry conditions
The material exhibits weak H2O adsorption ability and strong hydrothermal stability
The material has a lower formation energy of oxygen vacancies, which improves its catalytic performance
item.mechanism: The high entropy structure of the material leads to a lower Gibbs free energy, which enhances its stability and water resistance. The material's surface has a weaker H2O adsorption ability, which reduces the competitive adsorption with C3H6 and improves its catalytic performance.
item.future_work: Further exploration of the capabilities of high entropy oxide materials in heterogeneous catalysis and the development of new materials for water-resistant catalysis
quotes: Herein, a concept of engineering entropy to design water-resistant oxide catalysts is proposed
The strategy of adjusting entropy in oxides may be beneficial for catalysis under water-resistant conditions

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high entropy oxide materials be designed to be water-resistant and exhibit excellent catalytic performance?. System: High entropy oxide materials, specifically (Ni0.2Mg0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2Co0.2)Cr2O4. Processing: Mechanochemical method using ball milling, followed by calcination at 550 °C for 2 h. Test conditions: C3H6 oxidation reaction in dry and humid conditions (4.2 vol% H2O). Findings: High entropy oxide materials exhibit better water resistance and catalytic performance compared to single metal oxides; The (Ni0.2Mg0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2Co0.2)Cr2O4 material shows excellent water resistance (>100 h) in C3H6 oxidation; The material has a lower T90 (265 °C) compared to single metal oxides (318-350 °C) in dry conditions; The material exhibits weak H2O adsorption ability and strong hydrothermal stability; The material has a lower formation energy of oxygen vacancies, which improves its catalytic performance. Mechanism: The high entropy structure of the material leads to a lower Gibbs free energy, which enhances its stability and water resistance. The material's surface has a weaker H2O adsorption ability, which reduces the competitive adsorption with C3H6 and improves its catalytic performance.. Future work: Further exploration of the capabilities of high entropy oxide materials in heterogeneous catalysis and the development of new materials for water-resistant catalysis. Quote: "Herein, a concept of engineering entropy to design water-resistant oxide catalysts is proposed"
